- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show strong mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes; model tends to overreact and peak too high, then corrects too slowly.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually converges toward true mean.
- When true values show strong downward momentum after a spike, model fails to adjust quickly enough — underestimates the drop.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility, leading to overconfidence in short-term directionality.
- In periods of high volatility, model often fails to capture the true mean reversion speed — forecasts lag behind actual mean reversion.
- When true values are clustered around a low range, model tends to overestimate the next value, especially if recent history was high.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks in the short term, leading to delayed correction.
- Model often fails to account for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns — e.g., price dips in late Q4 or early Q1.
